subject: Post-call recap — PayFlux inference cost qualification & next steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@payflux.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — PayFlux inference cost qualification & next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for the 30-minute intro earlier. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment on pain, goals, and the cost levers we discussed. I kept this focused so we can share with your finance and infra teams.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Rapid cost growth on existing vendor as usage scales (unexpected spikes in verification flows).
- High tail latency during batch settlement windows; engineering time to tune ops.
- Need to keep sensitive transaction context in-house (data residency/compliance questions).

Goals you outlined:
- Reduce inference spend for verification flows by ~30% year-over-year while preserving model quality.
- Achieve sub-200ms P95 for single-turn checks and acceptable batch throughput for settlement windows.
- Pilot in a VPC/private mode first (security review already in progress).

Quick cost sketch (rough numbers we discussed):
- Estimated usage (your provided): ~150M tokens / month (verification + enrichment).
- Baseline hosted inference estimate (rough): ~$3,750/month at ~ $0.025 per 1k tokens (this is a quick benchmark for the goal-setting exercise).
- Primary levers we can apply: batching (continuous batching across short windows), prefix/KV caching for repeated context, and quantized model variants for lower-cost throughput.
- Combined conservative savings estimate: 30–40% on token spend if we enable batching + caching + a quantized 8-bit model path for verification flows. That maps to ~$1.1k–$1.5k/month in savings on the 150M token baseline; exacts depend on sequence length and hit rate on cache.

Recommended pilot (proposed):
1) 6-week scoped pilot focused on verification pipeline only (core KPIs: $/verified event, P95 latency, cache hit rate).
2) Two model variants: high-accuracy (float32) for edge cases + low-cost quantized variant for steady-state traffic.
3) Batching profile: start conservative (batch window 20–50 ms) and tune — we expect 20–30% latency-friendly savings early.
4) KV/prefix caching for repeated customer context — target 10–20% additional token reduction depending on reuse.
5) Weekly check-ins; final TCO model and recommendation at the end.

Next steps / asks from PayFlux:
- Please share a small sample of anonymized verification traffic (example logs or tokenized prompt samples) for sizing — we can handle sanitized exports.
- Confirm budget guardrails for the pilot (what monthly spend ceiling do you want to hit during the pilot?).
- Proposed follow-up: 30 mins on Tue 4/6 to review the initial TCO workbook and align on pilot SLOs.

Attachments: payflux_pilot_tco_v1.xlsx (TCO workbook), redwood_batching_profiles.pdf (short note on batching/caching levers).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the anonymized sample and suggested budget ceiling, then I’ll schedule the 4/6 slot.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[chloe.martin@redwood.ai] | +1 415-555-0192
From: Priya Singh <priya@payflux.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finance <finance@payflux.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — PayFlux inference cost qualification & next steps

Thanks Chloe — this is super helpful and aligns with what I was taking away. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Verification traffic: the 150M tokens/month is our median for verification flows; peak settlement windows push burst traffic up ~3x for ~15 mins/day.
2) Budget guardrail: for the pilot team-level spend, keep it under $10k total across 6 weeks unless we explicitly approve overrun.

We can deliver an anonymized sample of tokenized prompts by Monday morning. Would prefer the 4/6 time but can do 4/7 if that works better for your team.

Also, Marissa from your side — please confirm whether the quantized model path will require additional compliance paperwork for a VPC deployment.

Best,
Priya Singh
Head of Product (Payments) | PayFlux
priya@payflux.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@payflux.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — PayFlux inference cost qualification & next steps

@Chloe — quick note: quantized paths (8-bit) are available in private deployments and generally do not change the compliance surface; they are an execution detail in the runtime. We will loop in Security for a short readout but I don’t expect extra legal paperwork beyond standard VPC onboarding.

I’ve attached the short batching profile slide we use for sizing — it should help Priya’s team estimate hit rates.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
[marissa.cole@redwood.ai]
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@payflux.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — PayFlux inference cost qualification & next steps

Thanks Priya — appreciate the quick confirmations. To close the loop:

Action items I’ll take (Chloe):
- I’ll schedule the 30-min TCO review for Tue 2027-04-06 10:00am PT (tentative) and send a calendar invite — Priya, I’ll mark as flexible to 4/7 if you prefer.
- Prep a pre-filled TCO tab in the workbook using the anonymized sample once you share it; initial numbers ready within 24 hours of sample receipt.
- Provide a short runbook for the pilot (SLA targets, instrumentation hooks we’ll need for cost/latency measurement).

Action items for PayFlux (Priya):
- Share anonymized prompt samples and a 7-day sample of peak window traffic by end of day Mon 4/5.
- Confirm the $10k pilot ceiling or raise an alternative.

Avery will coordinate the engineering kickoff and instrumentation checklist once we have the sample. Marissa will be on the 4/6 call to run through batching/cache assumptions.

If that all looks good I’ll send the invite and attach the TCO workbook that includes a simple sensitivity table for cache hit rate (0–40%) and batching savings (0–35%).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to running this with you.

Chloe Martin
